I'm thinking through how to approach this.


The user wants to replicate a TV-optimized UI, specifically referencing an existing open-source project as a model. Analysis of the example project reveals key UI patterns common to TV interfaces: hero sections, horizontal card carousels, and left navigation rails optimized for 10-foot viewing. The goal is to produce code adhering to these design principles.


Card focus will utilize scaling and visual effects such as glowing borders to signal selection, alongside smooth auto-scrolling to maintain centered alignment. API integration involves fetching trending, popular movie/TV data, and detailed item information from an external movie database, using specific endpoints. Existing on-device streaming proxy remains to maintain uninterrupted video playback capabilities.


HTML structure will encompass a left navigation rail, a main viewport with hero billboard and content rows, along with modal overlays for detailed views and video playback. TV-optimized CSS utilizes a fixed 1920x1080 canvas, overscan padding, focus scaling with glow effects, and a cinema dark theme. The TMDB API service will fetch trending, movie, and TV data. Spatial navigation handles row-based focus and LG remote back button events.
